commits.edited_message:
ar: Add Windows Archive file support

Archives in ar format as written by Windows tools like lib.exe, separate
strings in string table directly with \0 instead of /\n.

GNU ar translates backslashes into slashes before the /\n check.

Handle both for improved compatibility, which also allows ar archives to
contain files in a directory structure.

An odd-sized filename table is stored with a one-byte pad so the next
member stays even-aligned. Keep that byte addressable and let the
separator scan see it, so a separator on the last payload byte is
handled the same way as one in the middle of the table.

Resolves #546

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

ar: Always skip all special entry bytes

The special file entries / and // are supposed to be properly padded,
but don't implicitly rely on it. Use archive_read_format_ar_skip
instead which takes care of possible padding bytes.

archive_read_format_ar_skip() clears entry_padding after consuming the
pad. The filename-table separator scan still consults that flag, so
restore it once the entry has been skipped.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

coupling: 639f5c4 makes an odd GNU filename table's trailing pad addressable (one extra allocated byte) and teaches ar_parse_gnu_filename_table to scan one byte further when entry_padding == 1, so a '/' on the last payload byte is handled like a mid-table '/\n'. That is safe on its own: the extra byte is allocated, and until the later rewrite entry_padding is still 1 during the scan. 6526406 switches the '//' member to archive_read_format_ar_skip(), which consumes the pad and clears entry_padding; the rewritten allocator keeps malloc(strtab_size) and therefore drops the extra byte, while the edit restores entry_padding after the skip so the earlier scan still runs. Restoring the flag alone does nothing to the original loop, which never reads past strtab_size-1, and the longer scan alone never runs once skip() has cleared the flag. The out-of-bounds read appears only when the restored flag, the extended walk, and the exact-size buffer are all present. Keeping both behaviors (odd-table separator scan and skip-based consumption) means putting the extra byte back in the post-skip allocator or stopping the walk at strtab_size; either repair has to look at the other commit's change.
